basis: Defining sensorineural deafness, intestinal aganglionosis and skin/hair hypopigmentation; iris pigmentation does not imply ocular damage.
Septo-optic dysplasia with defining digital anomalies; pituitary hormone deficiency occurs in roughly 60-80% of septo-optic dysplasia.
Umbrella for intrinsic immune deficiency; no additional organ damage applies consistently across the group.
Congenital ventricular septal defect with aortic cusp prolapse and regurgitation; dyspnea reflects cardiac dysfunction.
Benign neoplasm arising in the renal cortex.
Defining skeletal dysplasia; myopia, hearing impairment and cleft palate each occur in 30-79%. Retinal detachment and cataract are less frequent.

Progressive destructive brainstem and white-matter disease; vomiting and abnormal eye movements do not establish separate GI or ocular damage.

Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining lactic acidosis, encephalopathy and structural brain damage; respiratory distress alone does not prove lung damage.

Malignant smooth-muscle tumor arising in the colon; visceral smooth-muscle origin does not establish locomotor muscle involvement.

Inherited renal tubular electrolyte-handling disorders causing hyperkalemia and acid-base abnormalities; additional features vary by subtype.
Defining brain degeneration, cataracts/microphthalmia and contractures; hearing impairment 30-79%. Hypogonadism, also 30-79%, omitted by cap.
High-flow vascular malformation occupying the mandible with jaw and dental distortion; bleeding alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; optic atrophy reported in one assessed patient does not establish involvement in at least 30% overall.
Inherited platelet deficiency; significant immunodeficiency is not defining for isolated X-linked thrombocytopenia, and dermatitis frequency is unspecified.
Respiratory motile-cilia dysfunction with bronchiectasis; intrinsic middle-ear clearance dysfunction causes common chronic otitis, reported in 2/2 patients.
Usually phenotypically silent; supplied organ phenotypes reflect separate recessive diseases unmasked by homozygosity, not intrinsic effects of this UPD.
Defining retinal dystrophy, hearing loss and insulin resistance; cardiomyopathy occurs in ~60%. Progressive renal and hepatic disease omitted by cap.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction disorder; weakness, ptosis, dysphagia and respiratory insufficiency reflect impaired neuromuscular transmission.
Inherited generalized epilepsy with febrile and afebrile seizures; no established additional organ damage.
Disease of teeth, explicitly assigned to the gastrointestinal axis; skeletal ontology ancestry does not add musculoskeletal involvement.
Defining cataracts, ataxia and intellectual disability; short stature and hypotonia alone do not establish skeletal or primary muscle disease.
